stories.title: SingleCell-ArthritisNet: multitask prediction of cell type, sample source, and marker-defined transcriptional state in arthritis scRNA-seq
stories.description: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data poses challenges for simultaneously characterizing cell identity, sample source, and inflammatory transcriptional states in cellular heterogeneity of arthritis. We created a multitask shared-encoder framework called SingleCell-ArthritisNet, which can predict cell type, tissue/sample source, and a marker-defined transcriptional proxy. It was tested on 284,323 unique cells of 19 harmonized groups of biological samples under 5-fold donor/sample-group-disjoint cross validation, with one prediction per cell. Across folds, cell-type accuracy and macro-F1 were 0.8553 ± 0.0584 and 0.7642 ± 0.0281, respectively, while tissue/sample-source accuracy and macro-F1 were 0.9507 ± 0.0138 and 0.9453 ± 0.0169. For the marker-defined transcriptional proxy, fold-mean F1, AUPR, and AUROC were 0.8472 ± 0.0662, 0.9147 ± 0.0567, and 0.9850 ± 0.0046, respectively. The multitask model had only a small advantage in pooled cell-type macro-F1 (difference = 0.0069; 95% CI: 0.0016–0.0102; unadjusted p = 0.0040) and similar macro-F1 for the tissues and sample sources but lower proxy F1 and AUPR. Such comparisons are indicative of benefits at the task level, not of general predictive superiority. The marker-defined target mimics an expression-based thresholding rule and does not define colocalization between cells or a physical NK–cDC1 niche on its own. The accuracy and macro-F1 of external evaluation with 56,048 cells in 8 matched labels were 0.6129 and 0.4057, respectively. These results confirm the applicability of this framework for multitask prediction within a cohort and emphasize the need to appropriately preprocess the data, map it to the ontology, and validate the target cohort to ensure that the model can be used with a new dataset.

stories.title: Geochemical characteristics and organic matter enrichment mechanisms of early Cambrian Black Shales in the Northern Lower Yangtze Region, Eastern China
stories.description: During the Early Cambrian, a widespread suite of organic-rich black shale sequences was deposited in the Yangtze Block, offering a critical archive for understanding global oceanic chemical evolution and mineral cycles. However, the mechanisms and controlling factors governing organic matter enrichment in these deposits remain debated. This study integrates geochemical parameters—including total organic carbon (TOC) content, major and trace elements, and rare earth element concentrations—from 38 core samples of the Lower Cambrian Mufushan Formation in the northern Lower Yangtze region to reconstruct paleoproductivity and paleo-oceanic conditions, thereby elucidating the primary drivers of organic matter accumulation. The results demonstrate that the black shales possess high organic matter abundance (TOC up to 26.1%). Phosphorus/aluminum ratios and biogenic barium (Babio) concentrations reveal moderate to high paleoproductivity. Redox-sensitive trace element ratios (e.g., V/(V + Ni) up to 0.93) consistently indicate that the water column was predominantly characterized by anoxic and reducing conditions. Notably, both productivity and redox conditions exhibit a pronounced “strong-weak-strong” trend from the base to the top of the formation, which shows a positive correlation with organic matter abundance. Although productivity remained relatively high and stable at the top, the coupling of elevated paleoproductivity with strongly reducing conditions facilitated the formation of the most organic-rich intervals at both the top and bottom of the succession, indicating that the synergy between high productivity and efficient preservation was the fundamental mechanism controlling organic matter enrichment in the Early Cambrian ocean of the Lower Yangtze region.

stories.title: Machine learning-based 3D point cloud segmentation for scalable solute cluster analysis in atom probe tomography
stories.description: Accurate quantification of nanoscale solute cluster populations is essential for establishing structure–property relationships in radiation-damaged structural alloys. Atom probe tomography (APT) delivers the three-dimensional elemental and spatial resolution required for this characterization, but the analysis of large reconstructions containing hundreds of millions of ions remains a critical bottleneck. Conventional cluster analysis in APT relies on two principal approaches. Commercial software packages offer iso-concentration surfaces. These are effective for visualizing large, well-separated precipitates. However, they are sensitive to voxel size and concentration threshold and perform poorly on small, dilute, or closely spaced clusters. The software also offers the maximum separation method. This method can yield quantitative cluster statistics. However, it requires multiple self-determined input parameters and is inherently subjective. Density-based alternatives such as HDBSCAN address some of these limitations but scale quadratically with dataset size through pairwise distance computations and become statistically unstable under the severe class imbalance characteristic of heavily irradiated specimens, where cluster atoms constitute only a small fraction of the total reconstruction. We present a two-stage workflow decoupling foreground segmentation done by machine learning from density-based clustering called SegAPT-3D. A transformer-based model pre-trained on a synthetic APT generator first suppresses the solid-solution matrix and isolates candidate cluster-forming ions; HDBSCAN is then applied to this denoised foreground. On Fe–Cr datasets spanning Cr percentages from 9% to 18%, SegAPT-3D recovers cluster number densities, volume fractions, and average radii consistent with published reference values, with uncertainties that do not grow with foreground concentration, while reducing runtime by more than 24$$\times$$ on the largest reconstructions. Evaluation on neutron irradiated reactor pressure vessel steel and neutron irradiated HT9 steel that were not part of the training dataset demonstrates that learned representations can transfer across alloy chemistry without specimen-specific supervision, providing a scalable foundation for high-throughput characterization of irradiated materials. The segmentation model (SegAPT-3D) used in this study are publicly available at https://github.com/idaholab/SegAPT-3D.

stories.description: The 30,000-square-meter site will produce AL and AXION compressors for food retail and food service and house engineering and laboratory operations.

stories.title: Todoist Breach Exposes Legacy Password Hashes
stories.description: Todoist says a breach exposed emails and legacy password hashes for about 6% of users. See what happened and when to reset passwords or replace API tokens.
